intended_object: For a topological pair (X, A) and a family U of subsets of X, the sub-simplicial set S^U(X) ⊆ S(X) of the singular simplicial set of the ambient space X. It consists of the singular simplices σ : Δⁿ → X whose image lies in some U_i (the "U-small" simplices of Hatcher §2.1, Prop. 2.21), viewed as a subcomplex of the ambient part of the singular pair of (X, A). This reading comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition just re-types `TopCat.smallSingularSubcomplex` applied to the ambient space `P.fst`.

That underlying definition takes, in each degree n, the simplices σ with `∃ i, Set.range σ ⊆ U i`. It shows closure under the simplicial structure maps by naturality: a face or degeneracy of σ has image inside the image of σ. This is exactly the standard U-small singular complex.

`P.fst` is the ambient space of the pair. The preimage lemma that follows confirms this: pulling back along `P.map : P.snd → P.fst` gives the small subcomplex of the subspace for the family `P.map ⁻¹' U i`. The definition compiles with type `(toSSetPair.obj P).right.Subcomplex`, so the ambient simplicial set of the singular pair is the one the subcomplex lives in, as the docstring states.

It asks for no openness or covering condition, and the docstring of `TopCat.smallSingularSubcomplex` says none is needed for the definition. This matches the literature, where those hypotheses only enter the small-chain theorem. Arbitrary index types and arbitrary families of subsets are allowed, which is the natural generality.

Mathlib has no notion of U-small singular simplices, so there is no counterpart.
